findings.description: The inline user policy grants full wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on Resource "*", violating least privilege. Compromise of this user's credentials would allow full control of compute, all bucket data, arbitrary Lambda code execution (a privilege-escalation path via lambda:CreateFunction with an existing execution role), and deletion of CloudWatch logs to destroy audit evidence.

A static IAM access key is created with no pgp_key argument, so the plaintext secret access key is stored unencrypted in the Terraform state file and is retrievable by anyone with state access. These non-rotating long-term credentials are attached to the highly privileged excess_policy, so leakage of state is equivalent to full account compromise; IAM roles with temporary credentials should be used instead.

The configuration declares output "secret" exposing the access key secret material (and output "username"). Root-module outputs are persisted in state and printed to the console/CI logs, propagating the credential to build logs and any consumer of the module.

The IAM user is created without a permissions_boundary and with no MFA or password policy constraint, so nothing caps the effective privileges granted by the attached wildcard policy. In a regulated environment an IAM role assumed by a workload should be used rather than a standing user with static keys.
